metaDescription: Six 2200 watt class inverter generators compared on true running watts, outlets, noise, fuel options and service support for RV, jobsite and home backup.
expertTake: The Honda EU2200i is still the benchmark for people who want a machine that starts every time and has a dealer behind it. The Westinghouse iGen2800DFc is the value pick because it states 2200 running watts and adds propane. If you only need a lantern and phone charging, a 2200 watt machine is more engine than you need.
introParagraphs: This class sits just above the entry level, where a small inverter generator starts to handle a real RV load or a short outage backup. Machines here usually give you a bit more running margin and a proper RV outlet than the smaller tier below.

Labels in this class are slippery. The headline figure can mean maximum, running or even a listing typo, so the real comparison is what each machine will hold for hours, how loud it gets under load and who services it in year three.

products.name: Honda EU2200i 2200W Inverter Generator
products.description:
The EU2200i is the reference design for this class. Honda pairs its own four-stroke engine with an inverter module and a sound-damped case, and the listing promises quiet running that starts near the 48 dBA range at light load.

The label says 2200 watts maximum, which on Honda's data plate means about 1800 running. That is lower than the Westinghouse at 2200 running on gasoline, so on paper the Honda is the weaker pick for pure power. You pay for engineering consistency, a service network and a machine that tends to keep a high resale value after a decade.

Ownership is where it earns the ranking. Parts like carburetor kits, filters and plugs are stocked at dealers, the manual is clear, and a fuel valve lets you run the carburetor dry before storage. It suits buyers who keep a generator for years and want the least drama, and it is a poor fit for anyone who needs to power a heavy tool or a 15,000 BTU air conditioner.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want the most proven machine and dealer support.
pros: Honda engine with a long service record
Sound-damped case for low noise at light load
Strong resale and parts availability
Easy fuel valve routine for storage
cons: Running output is about 1800 watts, below the 2200 label
Costs more than unbranded rivals with similar specs

products.name: Honda EU2200i Companion 2200W
products.description:
The Companion variant takes the same engine as the base EU2200i and adds a built-in 30 amp outlet, which makes RV hookups and parallel use more convenient. Honda also lists its My Generator app over Bluetooth for remote start and monitoring.

The RV outlet is the real reason to pick it. Plugging a camper shore cord into a standard 20 amp receptacle needs an adapter, which is one more connector to fail. Against the plain EU2200i the Companion costs more, so buy it only if you have a 30 amp camper or plan to run two Honda units together.

The ownership notes match the base model. Use fresh fuel, change oil on schedule and shut the fuel valve before storage. Its weakness is the same as the EU2200i, running output near 1800 watts, which makes it the wrong choice for a household with a window air conditioner.
products.bestFor: RV owners who want a direct 30 amp outlet and an app.
pros: Built-in 30 amp outlet for camper cords
Bluetooth app for remote operation
Easier parallel setup with a second Honda
Same proven engine as the base model
cons: Higher cost than the standard EU2200i
The 2200 label hides roughly 1800 running watts

products.name: Westinghouse iGen2800DFc Dual Fuel Inverter
products.description:
This is the only machine here that states 2200 running watts on gasoline, with 2800 peak behind it. It also runs on propane, and carries both a 30 amp TT-30R RV outlet and a 20 amp household outlet.

That gives it about 400 more running watts than the Honda EU2200i, which is the difference between running a small air conditioner with margin and tripping the breaker. Propane operation will reduce output, a normal trade on dual fuel units, and you should check the manual for the exact figure before relying on it for a heavy load.

The cost is brand maturity. Westinghouse has a good dealer footprint for generators, but a newer inverter lineup will not have Honda's long record. Treat it as a strong value machine and keep a spare plug and filter on the shelf. It suits owners who want an RV-ready unit with real running margin and the option to burn propane.
products.bestFor: RV owners who want real running watts and dual fuel.
pros: States 2200 running watts on gasoline
Dual fuel gives a stable storage option
30 amp RV outlet plus a 20 amp outlet
Eco mode trims fuel use at light load
cons: Propane output is lower than gasoline output
Shorter track record than Honda inverters

products.name: Honda EB2200i OSHA-Compliant Inverter
products.description:
The EB2200i is the contractor version of the same quiet Honda platform. It adds full GFCI protection on the outlets, which is what makes it acceptable on many commercial worksites where ground-fault protection is required.

For a homeowner this is the model you buy if you run power tools outdoors in damp conditions, because the GFCI trips fast when a cord is damaged. The tradeoff is that GFCI protection can nuisance trip with older tools that leak a little current, and it adds cost versus the EU2200i with no gain in power.

Ownership matches the EU series: same engine, same fuel and oil routine, same dealer network. Choose it if you hire out or work around moisture, and skip it if your only use is camping, where the extra protection costs more than it returns.
products.bestFor: Contractors and tool users who need GFCI protected outlets.
pros: Full GFCI protection on the outlets
OSHA-compliant design for commercial work
Same quiet Honda engine platform
Reliable parts and dealer service
cons: Costs more than the EU2200i with equal output
GFCI can trip on leaky older tools

products.name: WEN 56235i 2350W Inverter Generator
products.description:
WEN lists 1900 rated watts, which is actually higher than the roughly 1800 running watts of a Honda EU2200i, and at 39 pounds it is lighter than the Honda. Those two facts make it the main price-conscious alternative in this tier.

It does not match the Honda on dealer reach or on resale, and it has no 30 amp RV outlet, so you need a 20 amp to 30 amp adapter for a camper. For the rest, it covers phones, laptops, a fridge and lights, and the fuel shut off valve makes seasonal storage easy.

The practical advice is to buy it if you want the running margin and the lighter weight, and be disciplined about oil changes. A small crankcase in this price band is worth checking before every outing, since the low-oil shutdown stops the job mid-use.
products.bestFor: Shoppers who want more rated watts than a Honda for less money.
pros: 1900 rated watts beats the Honda running figure
Lighter at 39 pounds than most rivals here
Fuel shut off valve for easy storage
Clean power for sensitive devices

products.name: 2200W Parallel-Ready Inverter Generator with CO Sensor
products.description:
This unbranded unit carries a CO sensor, eco mode and parallel readiness, features usually found on pricier machines. The title says 2200 watts but the text says 2000 watts, so treat the output as 2000 class until you see the data plate.

The tradeoff is weight and certainty. At 41.2 pounds it is heavier than the WEN by about 2 pounds, and with no named manufacturer the warranty and parts path are the risk. Use eco mode for light loads such as fans and chargers and switch it off before a pump or fridge compressor starts.

It is a sensible choice for someone who values a safety sensor and the option to add a second machine. Keep the receipt and photograph the data plate to hold the seller to the stated rating.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a CO sensor and parallel capability at a lower cost.
pros: CO sensor included in the listing
Eco mode extends runtime on light loads
Parallel ready for a second unit
Weighs 41.2 pounds for a portable carry
cons: Title and text disagree on 2200 versus 2000 watts
Unbranded parts and warranty path is uncertain

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 2200 label usually means maximum output, not what the engine holds. The Honda EU2200i is about 1800 running while the Westinghouse states 2200 running on gasoline and the WEN lists 1900 rated. Add up your loads using nameplate running watts and shop by the rated figure. A 400 watt gap decides whether a small air conditioner works.

A 30 amp TT-30R outlet lets a camper plug in directly. The Honda Companion and Westinghouse have one; the base EU2200i, EB2200i and WEN rely on 20 amp receptacles. Adapters add a failure point and can limit current, so buy the outlet you need if you own a camper.

Honda lists its quiet range starting near 48 dBA, but that is at light load. As load rises, the engine speeds up and the sound climbs. The eco mode on the Westinghouse and generic 2200W unit helps at light load only, so rely on the number as a ranking, not a promise.

Gasoline is the easiest fuel to find but goes stale in storage. The Westinghouse iGen2800DFc adds propane, which stores for years but cuts output. If your generator sits for most of the year, dual fuel can mean the difference between starting and not starting after two winters.

The Honda EB2200i adds full GFCI protection, which many commercial worksites require. For home camping use, the standard outlet is fine. Buy the GFCI model if you work around wet ground, and skip it if older tools nuisance trip.

Honda dealers stock carburetor kits, filters and plugs for the EU and EB series. Westinghouse has a service presence, WEN sells parts online and the unbranded unit leaves you on your own. In year three, parts access can matter more than the starting price.

specDecoder.meaning: Usually the maximum short-term output. The continuous figure sits lower, often by 15 to 20 percent.
specDecoder.watchFor: The EU2200i and EB2200i run about 1800 continuous, so never size to the 2200 figure.

specDecoder.meaning: What the engine can hold for hours. This is the number to compare with appliance labels.
specDecoder.watchFor: Westinghouse at 2200 running and WEN at 1900 rated both beat the Honda's running figure.

specDecoder.meaning: A 120V 30 amp camper receptacle. It allows a direct RV shore cord connection.
specDecoder.watchFor: Only the Westinghouse and Honda Companion in this lineup list it.

specDecoder.meaning: The engine speed follows the load instead of running at a fixed speed. It saves fuel and noise at light load.
specDecoder.watchFor: Turn it off when a compressor or pump starts, as the engine needs time to respond.

specDecoder.meaning: A device that cuts power in milliseconds if current leaks to ground. It is a safety feature for wet or tool use.
specDecoder.watchFor: The EB2200i adds it, and older tools with leaky motors may trip it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Real running output
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated stated running watts and discounted a bare maximum figure. The Westinghouse at 2200 running led, the WEN at 1900 rated followed, and the Honda units at about 1800 landed after them. Listings with no rated figure were marked down.

howWeEvaluated.title: Outlets and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared RV and jobsite fit from the spec sheet. A 30 amp outlet and GFCI protection each earned credit for the right buyer. Adapter-dependent units lost points for RV use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise and weight
howWeEvaluated.description: We read stated decibel figures and weights as rankings only. The WEN at 39 pounds is lighter than the generic unit at 41.2. Honda's quiet range starting near 48 dBA stays a light-load claim.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fuel and storage
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed how each fuel setup handles a long idle period. Dual fuel on the Westinghouse earned credit, as did a fuel shut off on the WEN and the Hondas. Gasoline-only units with no shutoff would lose points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Service and ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We used owner feedback patterns on parts and dealer support. Honda scored highest for dealer reach, with Westinghouse and WEN behind it. The unbranded unit scored lowest for support clarity.

rows: High rated watts for the price
More running watts and dual fuel

cards.label: Honda EU and EB
cards.text: The Honda machines give you a proven engine, dealer parts and strong resale, but only about 1800 running watts. They suit people who keep a generator for ten years and value reliability over power per dollar.

cards.label: Westinghouse, WEN and the generic unit
cards.text: These offer more stated running watts or more features, such as dual fuel on the Westinghouse and a CO sensor on the generic unit. You trade dealer reach and resale for power per dollar.

howToChoose.note: Long-term keepers should choose Honda; shoppers who need extra running margin should choose the Westinghouse or WEN.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Check the air conditioner's running and starting amps, then confirm the generator holds the running figure plus startup. A small 5,000 BTU unit needs far more than the label watts suggest at the moment the compressor starts.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Westinghouse iGen2800DFc at 2200 running watts is the only pick with enough steady margin. The Honda EU2200i at about 1800 running will struggle at startup.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You plan to keep the machine for a decade or own a 30 amp RV. The Honda EU2200i Companion earns its price through parts support and a direct RV outlet.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You mostly need phones, lights and a fridge a few days a year. The WEN 56235i delivers 1900 rated watts for less than the Honda.

maintenance.interval: First 20 hours, then yearly or every 100 hours
maintenance.why: The crankcase is tiny and runs hot. Fresh oil prevents wear and low-oil shutdowns.
Dust cuts power and lengthens startup. Replace foam or paper elements when dirty.
A weak spark causes hard starts and wasted fuel. It costs very little to renew.

maintenance.task: Close the fuel valve and run dry
maintenance.why: This empties the carburetor bowl of ethanol fuel that gums jets. It is the best no-start prevention.

maintenance.task: Check the CO sensor and cords
maintenance.why: Sensors and cords degrade over time. Test them before depending on the unit during an outage.

faq.q: Is a Honda EU2200i worth the premium?
faq.a: If you keep a generator for years, yes, because of dealer parts and resale. If you want more running watts per dollar, the Westinghouse or WEN offer more on paper.

faq.q: Can a 2200 watt generator run a camper air conditioner?
faq.a: Only a small unit, and only if the generator holds enough steady watts. The Westinghouse with 2200 running watts has the margin, while the Honda at about 1800 running will struggle.

faq.q: What does the Companion add over the base EU2200i?
faq.a: A built-in 30 amp outlet and easier parallel use, plus the Bluetooth app listing. It is the better buy for 30 amp campers and a poor value for tent campers.

faq.q: Is 2200W the maximum or running figure?
faq.a: Usually the maximum. Always find the rated or running figure on the data plate or in the manual, since it can be about 400 watts lower.
No, but propane output is lower and you need to connect a regulator hose correctly. It does improve storage, since propane does not go stale.

faq.q: Do I need the GFCI model?
faq.a: Only for wet or commercial jobs where ground-fault protection is required. For camping and backup, the EU2200i is the simpler choice.
